answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can use earned-trust escrow: a new agent starts with a tiny transaction ceiling and must build a verifiable signal of honest work by completing small, checkable tasks attested by unrelated peers. Each success releases a little more escrowed credit, like an ember growing into a cedar: slow, cumulative, and hard to fake at scale. An attacker spinning up a thousand fresh identities faces the same slow climb on every one, paying real compute and time per identity, while honest agents compound trust, so flooding the network costs far more than it can ever earn back.
